70:1: Interpretation of Surat Al-Ma'arij In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful A questioner asked about a punishment to come true contains an implicit meaning indicated by the letter ba' as if it were understood. A questioner hastened the punishment to come true, as in the verse: And they urge you to hasten the punishment, but God will never fail in His promise. That is, His punishment will inevitably come true. An-Nasa'i said: Bishr ibn Khalid told us, Abu Usamah told us, Sufyan told us, from al-A'mash, from al-Minhal ibn Amr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: A questioner asked about a punishment to come true, An-Nadr ibn al-Harith ibn Kaladah said: Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas: A questioner asked about a punishment to come true, he said: That is the question of the disbelievers about God's punishment which is to come true upon them. Ibn Abi Nujayh said from Mujahid regarding the verse: A questioner asked, a supplicant prayed for a punishment to come true that will happen in the Hereafter. He said: It is their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. Ibn Zayd and others said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come true, meaning a valley in Hell that will flow with punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This statement is weak and far from the intended meaning, but the first is correct because the context indicates it. And the Almighty’s saying: It will come to pass * for the disbelievers meaning an ambush prepared for the disbelievers. Ibn Abbas said: It will come to pass and it has no repeller meaning there is no repeller for it if God wills it to be. For this reason the Almighty said: From God, the Possessor of the Ascending Stairways. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of a man on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways he said: Possessor of degrees. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways means the heights and bounties. Mujahid said: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways are the ascents to heaven. Qatada said: Possessor of the bounties and blessings. And the Almighty’s saying: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah: Ascends means ascends. As for the Spirit, Abu Salih said: They are a creation of God’s creation who resemble people, but they are not people. I said: It is possible that what is meant by it is Gabriel, and it is a case of connecting the specific to the general. It is possible that it is a generic name for the souls of the sons of Adam, for when they are taken, they ascend with them to the heavens, as indicated by the hadith of al-Bara’. In the hadith that Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of al-Minhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of al-Bara’, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, the hadith in its entirety about the taking of the pure soul, in which he said: He continues to ascend with it from one heaven to another until it reaches the heaven in which God is. And God knows best its authenticity. Some of its narrators have spoken about it, but it is well-known. It has a corroborating evidence in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as mentioned above, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on his authority. And this chain of transmission has men who meet the criteria of the group. We have expanded on its wording when he said: God Almighty says: “God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And God sends astray the wrongdoers, and God does what He wills.” And the Almighty’s saying: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years has four opinions: [One of them] is that what is meant by that is the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the low, which is the resting place of the seventh earth, and that is a journey of fifty thousand years. This is the elevation of the Throne from the center which is in the middle of the seventh earth, and likewise the expansion of the Throne from one diameter to another is a journey of fifty thousand years, and that it is made of a red ruby as Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned in the book Description of the Throne. Ibn Abi Hatim said about this verse: Ahmad bin Salamah told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Hakam told us, on the authority of Umar bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The extent of His command from the lowest of the earths to the extent of His command above the heavens is fifty thousand years. And indeed, a day with your Lord is as a thousand years of those which you count, meaning by that when the command descends from the heaven to the earth, and from the earth to the heavens in one day, so its extent is a thousand years because the distance between the heaven and the earth is the distance of a journey of five hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Hakam bin Salim, on the authority of Amr bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement was not mentioned by Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Nuh al-Mu’addib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and between each land and the next is five hundred years, so that is seven thousand years. The thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and between one heaven and the next is five hundred years, so that is four thousand years. And between the seventh heaven and the Throne is a journey of thirty-six thousand years, so that is what God Almighty said: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. The second statement that what is meant by that is the duration of the existence of this world from the time God created this world until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Ibn Abi Za’idah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The lifespan of this world is fifty thousand years, and that is its lifespan on the day that God Almighty called a day. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day, he said: The day is the world. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The world from its beginning to its end is the length of fifty thousand years. No one knows how much has passed and how much remains except God Almighty. The third statement is that it is the day separating this world from the hereafter, and this is a very strange statement. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us, Bahlol ibn al-Mawriq told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, Muhammad ibn Ka`b told me, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the day separating this world from the hereafter. The fourth opinion that what is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: The Day of Resurrection. Its chain of transmission is authentic. Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the Day of Resurrection. God the Almighty has made it for the disbelievers the extent of fifty thousand years. There are hadiths with the same meaning. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. How long is this day? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in this world. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj, with the same chain of transmission, except that Diraj and his sheikh, Abu Al-Haytham, are both weak, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu `Umar al-`Adani, who said: I was with Abu Hurairah when a man from Banu `Amir ibn Sa`sa`ah passed by. It was said to him, This is the richest of the `Amirs. Abu Hurairah said, Bring him back to me. So they did. He said, I have been told that you have much wealth. The `Amir said, Yes, by God, I have one hundred red camels and one hundred black camels. He counted the colors of camels, the types of slaves, and the tethers of horses. Abu Hurairah said, Beware of the hooves of camels and the hoofs of camels. He kept repeating this to him until the `Amir’s color changed. He said, What is that, O Abu Hurairah? He said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever has camels and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, we said: O Messenger of God, what is their rescue and their messengers?’ He said: ‘In their hardship and ease, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and they will trample him with their hooves. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has cows and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, then they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and every hoofed animal will trample him with its hoof and every horned animal will butt him with its horn. There is no ‘aqsa’ or ‘adhba’ among them. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has sheep and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, And its messengers, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, fat, and full, until a flat plain is spread out for them, and every hoofed animal will trample it with its hoof and every horned animal will butt it with its horn. There will be none among them who are crippled or twisted. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be returned to it in a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed between the people and he sees his way.” Al-Amiri said: What is the right of camels, O Abu Hurairah? He said: That you give to the generous and bestow, and that you make the back poor and give water to the camels and that you let the stallion ride on it. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, both of them from Qatadah with it. Another chain of transmission for this hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no owner of a treasure who does not pay its due except that plates will be made to be heated in the fire of Hell, and his forehead, sides, and back will be branded with them, until God judges between His servants on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years of what you count. Then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith about sheep and camels as mentioned above, and in it: “Horses are for three: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden,” to the end. Muslim narrated it in its entirety in his Sahih, alone, without al-Bukhari, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. The place for examining its chains of transmission and wording is in the Book of Zakat in the Book of Rulings. The purpose of citing it here is his saying: until God judges between His servants on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ibn Aliyah and Abd al-Wahhab on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah who said: A man asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said, What is a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years? He said, “So he accused him, and he said, ‘I only asked you so that you would tell me.’ He said, ‘They are two days that God mentioned, and God knows best about them, and I hate to say about the Book of God what I do not know.’” God the Almighty said: {So be patient with beautiful patience} meaning, O Muhammad, be patient with your people’s denial of you and their hastening the punishment, considering it unlikely to happen, as He said: {Those who do not believe in it urge it on, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth}. For this reason He said: {Indeed, they see it as far off}, meaning the occurrence of the punishment. The disbelievers see the occurrence of the Hour as far off, meaning impossible. {And We see it as near}, meaning the believers believe it is near, even though it has a time limit that only God the Almighty knows. But whatever it desires is near and will inevitably happen.

Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, concerning the words of God the Almighty: A questioner asked, a supplicant prayed for a punishment to come to pass in the Hereafter. He said: It is their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. Ibn Zayd and others said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass, meaning a valley in Hell that will flow with punishment on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abbas said: It will come to pass and it has no repeller meaning there is no repeller for it if God wills it to be. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of a man on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways he said: Possessor of degrees. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways means the heights and bounties. Mujahid said: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways are the ascents to heaven. Qatada said: Possessor of the bounties and blessings. And the Almighty’s saying: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah: Ascends means ascends. As for the Spirit, Abu Salih said: They are a creation of God’s creation who resemble people, but they are not people. It is possible that it is a generic name for the souls of the sons of Adam, for when they are taken, they ascend with them to the heavens, as indicated by the hadith of al-Bara’. And God knows best its authenticity. Some of its narrators have spoken about it, but it is well-known. It has a corroborating evidence in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as mentioned above, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on his authority. And this chain of transmission has men who meet the criteria of the group. We have expanded on its wording when he said: God Almighty says: “God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And God sends astray the wrongdoers, and God does what He wills.” And the Almighty’s saying: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years has four opinions: [One of them] is that what is meant by that is the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the low, which is the resting place of the seventh earth, and that is a journey of fifty thousand years. Ibn Abi Hatim said about this verse: Ahmad bin Salamah told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Hakam told us, on the authority of Umar bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The extent of His command from the lowest of the earths to the extent of His command above the heavens is fifty thousand years. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Nuh al-Mu’addib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and between each land and the next is five hundred years, so that is seven thousand years. The thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and between one heaven and the next is five hundred years, so that is four thousand years. And between the seventh heaven and the Throne is a journey of thirty-six thousand years, so that is what God Almighty said: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. The second statement that what is meant by that is the duration of the existence of this world from the time God created this world until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Ibn Abi Za’idah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The lifespan of this world is fifty thousand years, and that is its lifespan on the day that God Almighty called a day. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day, he said: The day is the world. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The world from its beginning to its end is the length of fifty thousand years. No one knows how much has passed and how much remains except God Almighty. The third statement is that it is the day separating this world from the hereafter, and this is a very strange statement. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us, Bahlol ibn al-Mawriq told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, Muhammad ibn Ka`b told me, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the day separating this world from the hereafter. The fourth opinion that what is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: The Day of Resurrection. Its chain of transmission is authentic. Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the Day of Resurrection. God the Almighty has made it for the disbelievers the extent of fifty thousand years. There are hadiths with the same meaning. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. How long is this day? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in this world. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj, with the same chain of transmission, except that Diraj and his sheikh, Abu Al-Haytham, are both weak, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu `Umar al-`Adani, who said: I was with Abu Hurairah when a man from Banu `Amir ibn Sa`sa`ah passed by. It was said to him, This is the richest of the `Amirs. Abu Hurairah said, Bring him back to me. So they did. He said, I have been told that you have much wealth. The `Amir said, Yes, by God, I have one hundred red camels and one hundred black camels. He counted the colors of camels, the types of slaves, and the tethers of horses. Abu Hurairah said, Beware of the hooves of camels and the hoofs of camels. He kept repeating this to him until the `Amir’s color changed. He said, What is that, O Abu Hurairah? He said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever has camels and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, we said: O Messenger of God, what is their rescue and their messengers?’ He said: ‘In their hardship and ease, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and they will trample him with their hooves. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has cows and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, then they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and every hoofed animal will trample him with its hoof and every horned animal will butt him with its horn. There is no ‘aqsa’ or ‘adhba’ among them. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has sheep and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, And its messengers, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, fat, and full, until a flat plain is spread out for them, and every hoofed animal will trample it with its hoof and every horned animal will butt it with its horn. There will be none among them who are crippled or twisted. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be returned to it in a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed between the people and he sees his way.” Al-Amiri said: What is the right of camels, O Abu Hurairah? He said: That you give to the generous and bestow, and that you make the back poor and give water to the camels and that you let the stallion ride on it. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, both of them from Qatadah with it. Then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith about sheep and camels as mentioned above, and in it: “Horses are for three: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden,” to the end. Muslim narrated it in its entirety in his Sahih, alone, without al-Bukhari, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. The place for examining its chains of transmission and wording is in the Book of Zakat in the Book of Rulings. The purpose of citing it here is his saying: until God judges between His servants on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ibn Aliyah and Abd al-Wahhab on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah who said: A man asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said, What is a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years? He said, “So he accused him, and he said, ‘I only asked you so that you would tell me.’ He said, ‘They are two days that God mentioned, and God knows best about them, and I hate to say about the Book of God what I do not know.’” God the Almighty said: {So be patient with beautiful patience} meaning, O Muhammad, be patient with your people’s denial of you and their hastening the punishment, considering it unlikely to happen, as He said: {Those who do not believe in it urge it on, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth}. For this reason He said: {Indeed, they see it as far off}, meaning the occurrence of the punishment. The disbelievers see the occurrence of the Hour as far off, meaning impossible. {And We see it as near}, meaning the believers believe it is near, even though it has a time limit that only God the Almighty knows. But whatever it desires is near and will inevitably happen.

Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, concerning the words of God the Almighty: A questioner asked, a supplicant prayed for a punishment to come to pass in the Hereafter. He said: It is their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. Ibn Zayd and others said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass, meaning a valley in Hell that will flow with punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This statement is weak and far from the intended meaning, but the first is correct because the context indicates it. Ibn Abbas said: It will come to pass and it has no repeller meaning there is no repeller for it if God wills it to be. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of a man on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways he said: Possessor of degrees. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways means the heights and bounties. Mujahid said: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways are the ascents to heaven. Qatada said: Possessor of the bounties and blessings. And the Almighty’s saying: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah: Ascends means ascends. As for the Spirit, Abu Salih said: They are a creation of God’s creation who resemble people, but they are not people. I said: It is possible that what is meant by it is Gabriel, and it is a case of connecting the specific to the general. It is possible that it is a generic name for the souls of the sons of Adam, for when they are taken, they ascend with them to the heavens, as indicated by the hadith of al-Bara’. In the hadith that Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of al-Minhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of al-Bara’, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, the hadith in its entirety about the taking of the pure soul, in which he said: He continues to ascend with it from one heaven to another until it reaches the heaven in which God is. And God knows best its authenticity. Some of its narrators have spoken about it, but it is well-known. It has a corroborating evidence in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as mentioned above, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on his authority. And this chain of transmission has men who meet the criteria of the group. We have expanded on its wording when he said: God Almighty says: “God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And God sends astray the wrongdoers, and God does what He wills.” And the Almighty’s saying: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years has four opinions: [One of them] is that what is meant by that is the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the low, which is the resting place of the seventh earth, and that is a journey of fifty thousand years. This is the elevation of the Throne from the center which is in the middle of the seventh earth, and likewise the expansion of the Throne from one diameter to another is a journey of fifty thousand years, and that it is made of a red ruby as Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned in the book Description of the Throne. Ibn Abi Hatim said about this verse: Ahmad bin Salamah told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Hakam told us, on the authority of Umar bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The extent of His command from the lowest of the earths to the extent of His command above the heavens is fifty thousand years. And indeed, a day with your Lord is as a thousand years of those which you count, meaning by that when the command descends from the heaven to the earth, and from the earth to the heavens in one day, so its extent is a thousand years because the distance between the heaven and the earth is the distance of a journey of five hundred years. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Nuh al-Mu’addib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and between each land and the next is five hundred years, so that is seven thousand years. The thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and between one heaven and the next is five hundred years, so that is four thousand years. And between the seventh heaven and the Throne is a journey of thirty-six thousand years, so that is what God Almighty said: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. The second statement that what is meant by that is the duration of the existence of this world from the time God created this world until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Ibn Abi Za’idah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The lifespan of this world is fifty thousand years, and that is its lifespan on the day that God Almighty called a day. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day, he said: The day is the world. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The world from its beginning to its end is the length of fifty thousand years. No one knows how much has passed and how much remains except God Almighty. The third statement is that it is the day separating this world from the hereafter, and this is a very strange statement. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us, Bahlol ibn al-Mawriq told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, Muhammad ibn Ka`b told me, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the day separating this world from the hereafter. The fourth opinion that what is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: The Day of Resurrection. Its chain of transmission is authentic. Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the Day of Resurrection. God the Almighty has made it for the disbelievers the extent of fifty thousand years. There are hadiths with the same meaning. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. How long is this day? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in this world. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj, with the same chain of transmission, except that Diraj and his sheikh, Abu Al-Haytham, are both weak, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu `Umar al-`Adani, who said: I was with Abu Hurairah when a man from Banu `Amir ibn Sa`sa`ah passed by. It was said to him, This is the richest of the `Amirs. Abu Hurairah said, Bring him back to me. So they did. He said, I have been told that you have much wealth. The `Amir said, Yes, by God, I have one hundred red camels and one hundred black camels. He counted the colors of camels, the types of slaves, and the tethers of horses. Abu Hurairah said, Beware of the hooves of camels and the hoofs of camels. He kept repeating this to him until the `Amir’s color changed. He said, What is that, O Abu Hurairah? He said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever has camels and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, we said: O Messenger of God, what is their rescue and their messengers?’ He said: ‘In their hardship and ease, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and they will trample him with their hooves. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has cows and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, then they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and every hoofed animal will trample him with its hoof and every horned animal will butt him with its horn. There is no ‘aqsa’ or ‘adhba’ among them. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has sheep and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, And its messengers, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, fat, and full, until a flat plain is spread out for them, and every hoofed animal will trample it with its hoof and every horned animal will butt it with its horn. There will be none among them who are crippled or twisted. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be returned to it in a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed between the people and he sees his way.” Al-Amiri said: What is the right of camels, O Abu Hurairah? He said: That you give to the generous and bestow, and that you make the back poor and give water to the camels and that you let the stallion ride on it. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, both of them from Qatadah with it. Then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith about sheep and camels as mentioned above, and in it: “Horses are for three: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden,” to the end. Muslim narrated it in its entirety in his Sahih, alone, without al-Bukhari, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. The place for examining its chains of transmission and wording is in the Book of Zakat in the Book of Rulings. The purpose of citing it here is his saying: until God judges between His servants on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ibn Aliyah and Abd al-Wahhab on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah who said: A man asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said, What is a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years? He said, “So he accused him, and he said, ‘I only asked you so that you would tell me.’ He said, ‘They are two days that God mentioned, and God knows best about them, and I hate to say about the Book of God what I do not know.’” God the Almighty said: {So be patient with beautiful patience} meaning, O Muhammad, be patient with your people’s denial of you and their hastening the punishment, considering it unlikely to happen, as He said: {Those who do not believe in it urge it on, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth}. For this reason He said: {Indeed, they see it as far off}, meaning the occurrence of the punishment. The disbelievers see the occurrence of the Hour as far off, meaning impossible. {And We see it as near}, meaning the believers believe it is near, even though it has a time limit that only God the Almighty knows. But whatever it desires is near and will inevitably happen.

Al-Nasa'i said: Bishr ibn Khalid told us, Abu Usamah told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Al-A'mash, on the authority of Al-Munhal ibn Amr, on the authority of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, concerning the words of God the Almighty: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass, Al-Nadr ibn Al-Harith ibn Kalda said: Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass, he said: This is the question of the disbelievers about the punishment of God which is to come to pass upon them. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid, concerning the words of God the Almighty: A questioner asked, a supplicant prayed for a punishment to come to pass in the Hereafter. He said: It is their saying: O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment. Ibn Zayd and others said: A questioner asked about a punishment to come to pass, meaning a valley in Hell that will flow with punishment on the Day of Resurrection. This statement is weak and far from the intended meaning, but the first is correct because the context indicates it. And the Almighty’s saying: It will come to pass * for the disbelievers meaning an ambush prepared for the disbelievers. Ibn Abbas said: It will come to pass and it has no repeller meaning there is no repeller for it if God wills it to be. For this reason the Almighty said: From God, the Possessor of the Ascending Stairways. Al-Thawri said on the authority of Al-A’mash on the authority of a man on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr on the authority of Ibn Abbas regarding the Almighty’s saying: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways he said: Possessor of degrees. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways means the heights and bounties. Mujahid said: Possessor of the Ascending Stairways are the ascents to heaven. Qatada said: Possessor of the bounties and blessings. And the Almighty’s saying: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him. Abd al-Razzaq said, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Qatadah: Ascends means ascends. As for the Spirit, Abu Salih said: They are a creation of God’s creation who resemble people, but they are not people. I said: It is possible that what is meant by it is Gabriel, and it is a case of connecting the specific to the general. It is possible that it is a generic name for the souls of the sons of Adam, for when they are taken, they ascend with them to the heavens, as indicated by the hadith of al-Bara’. In the hadith that Imam Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah narrated on the authority of al-Minhal, on the authority of Zadan, on the authority of al-Bara’, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, peace and blessings of God be upon him, the hadith in its entirety about the taking of the pure soul, in which he said: He continues to ascend with it from one heaven to another until it reaches the heaven in which God is. And God knows best its authenticity. Some of its narrators have spoken about it, but it is well-known. It has a corroborating evidence in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, as mentioned above, from the narration of Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, and Ibn Majah, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Yasar, on his authority. And this chain of transmission has men who meet the criteria of the group. We have expanded on its wording when he said: God Almighty says: “God confirms those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter. And God sends astray the wrongdoers, and God does what He wills.” And the Almighty’s saying: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years has four opinions: [One of them] is that what is meant by that is the distance between the Mighty Throne and the lowest of the low, which is the resting place of the seventh earth, and that is a journey of fifty thousand years. This is the elevation of the Throne from the center which is in the middle of the seventh earth, and likewise the expansion of the Throne from one diameter to another is a journey of fifty thousand years, and that it is made of a red ruby as Ibn Abi Shaybah mentioned in the book Description of the Throne. Ibn Abi Hatim said about this verse: Ahmad bin Salamah told us, Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Hakam told us, on the authority of Umar bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the words of God Almighty: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The extent of His command from the lowest of the earths to the extent of His command above the heavens is fifty thousand years. And indeed, a day with your Lord is as a thousand years of those which you count, meaning by that when the command descends from the heaven to the earth, and from the earth to the heavens in one day, so its extent is a thousand years because the distance between the heaven and the earth is the distance of a journey of five hundred years. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Hakam bin Salim, on the authority of Amr bin Maruf, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Mujahid, his statement was not mentioned by Ibn Abbas. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ali bin Muhammad al-Tanafisi told us, Ishaq bin Mansour told us, Nuh al-Mu’addib told us, on the authority of Abd al-Wahhab bin Mujahid, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The thickness of each earth is five hundred years, and between each land and the next is five hundred years, so that is seven thousand years. The thickness of each heaven is five hundred years, and between one heaven and the next is five hundred years, so that is four thousand years. And between the seventh heaven and the Throne is a journey of thirty-six thousand years, so that is what God Almighty said: In a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. The second statement that what is meant by that is the duration of the existence of this world from the time God created this world until the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Ibrahim bin Musa told us, Ibn Abi Za’idah told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God Almighty: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The lifespan of this world is fifty thousand years, and that is its lifespan on the day that God Almighty called a day. The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a Day, he said: The day is the world. Abd al-Razzaq said: Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Nujayh, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of al-Hakam bin Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah: On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years, he said: The world from its beginning to its end is the length of fifty thousand years. No one knows how much has passed and how much remains except God Almighty. The third statement is that it is the day separating this world from the hereafter, and this is a very strange statement. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya ibn Sa`id al-Qattan told us, Bahlol ibn al-Mawriq told us, Musa ibn Ubaydah told us, Muhammad ibn Ka`b told me, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the day separating this world from the hereafter. The fourth opinion that what is meant by this is the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan al-Wasiti told us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi told us, on the authority of Isra’il, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: The Day of Resurrection. Its chain of transmission is authentic. Ath-Thawri narrated it on the authority of Samak ibn Harb, on the authority of Ikrimah, On a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. Ad-Dahhak and Ibn Zayd said the same. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, regarding the verse: The angels and the Spirit ascend to Him during a Day the extent of which is fifty thousand years. He said: It is the Day of Resurrection. God the Almighty has made it for the disbelievers the extent of fifty thousand years. There are hadiths with the same meaning. Imam Ahmad said: Al-Hasan bin Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Diraj told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Haytham, on the authority of Abu Sa’id, who said: It was said to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, On a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. How long is this day? The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, it is made easy for the believer until it is lighter for him than an obligatory prayer that he prays in this world. And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Yunus, on the authority of Ibn Wahb, on the authority of Amr bin Al-Harith, on the authority of Diraj, with the same chain of transmission, except that Diraj and his sheikh, Abu Al-Haytham, are both weak, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja`far narrated to us, Shu`bah narrated to us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abu `Umar al-`Adani, who said: I was with Abu Hurairah when a man from Banu `Amir ibn Sa`sa`ah passed by. It was said to him, This is the richest of the `Amirs. Abu Hurairah said, Bring him back to me. So they did. He said, I have been told that you have much wealth. The `Amir said, Yes, by God, I have one hundred red camels and one hundred black camels. He counted the colors of camels, the types of slaves, and the tethers of horses. Abu Hurairah said, Beware of the hooves of camels and the hoofs of camels. He kept repeating this to him until the `Amir’s color changed. He said, What is that, O Abu Hurairah? He said: “I heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: ‘Whoever has camels and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, we said: O Messenger of God, what is their rescue and their messengers?’ He said: ‘In their hardship and ease, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and they will trample him with their hooves. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has cows and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, then they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, most numerous, fattest and most ravenous, then a plain of Qarqar will be spread out for them and every hoofed animal will trample him with its hoof and every horned animal will butt him with its horn. There is no ‘aqsa’ or ‘adhba’ among them. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be repeated to him on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed among the people and he sees his way. And if he has sheep and does not give them their due right in their rescue and their messengers, And its messengers, for they will come on the Day of Resurrection as they were most fertile, fat, and full, until a flat plain is spread out for them, and every hoofed animal will trample it with its hoof and every horned animal will butt it with its horn. There will be none among them who are crippled or twisted. When the last of them passes it, the first of them will be returned to it in a day the length of which will be fifty thousand years, until judgment is passed between the people and he sees his way.” Al-Amiri said: What is the right of camels, O Abu Hurairah? He said: That you give to the generous and bestow, and that you make the back poor and give water to the camels and that you let the stallion ride on it. Abu Dawud narrated it from the hadith of Shu’bah and al-Nasa’i from the hadith of Sa’id ibn Abi ‘Aruba, both of them from Qatadah with it. Another chain of transmission for this hadith Imam Ahmad said: Abu Kamil told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “There is no owner of a treasure who does not pay its due except that plates will be made to be heated in the fire of Hell, and his forehead, sides, and back will be branded with them, until God judges between His servants on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years of what you count. Then he will see his path, either to Paradise or to Hell.” And he mentioned the rest of the hadith about sheep and camels as mentioned above, and in it: “Horses are for three: for a man they are a reward, for a man they are a cover, and for a man they are a burden,” to the end. Muslim narrated it in its entirety in his Sahih, alone, without al-Bukhari, on the authority of Suhayl, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurairah. The place for examining its chains of transmission and wording is in the Book of Zakat in the Book of Rulings. The purpose of citing it here is his saying: until God judges between His servants on a day the length of which is fifty thousand years. And Ibn Jarir narrated on the authority of Ya’qub, on the authority of Ibn Aliyah and Abd al-Wahhab on the authority of Ayoub on the authority of Ibn Abi Malekah who said: A man asked Ibn Abbas about his statement, On a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years. He said, What is a Day the measure of which is fifty thousand years? He said, “So he accused him, and he said, ‘I only asked you so that you would tell me.’ He said, ‘They are two days that God mentioned, and God knows best about them, and I hate to say about the Book of God what I do not know.’” God the Almighty said: {So be patient with beautiful patience} meaning, O Muhammad, be patient with your people’s denial of you and their hastening the punishment, considering it unlikely to happen, as He said: {Those who do not believe in it urge it on, but those who believe are fearful of it and know that it is the truth}. For this reason He said: {Indeed, they see it as far off}, meaning the occurrence of the punishment. The disbelievers see the occurrence of the Hour as far off, meaning impossible. {And We see it as near}, meaning the believers believe it is near, even though it has a time limit that only God the Almighty knows. But whatever it desires is near and will inevitably happen.
70:8: God the Almighty says that the punishment will befall the disbelievers: On the Day when the sky will be like molten molten metal. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Ata’, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, As-Suddi and others said: That is, like the dregs of oil. And the mountains will be like carded wool. That is, like carded wool, said Mujahid, Qatadah and As-Suddi. This verse is like the Almighty’s saying: And the mountains will be like carded wool. And the Almighty’s saying: “And no close friend will ask a close friend. They will see them.” That is, a close relative will not ask his close relative about his condition while he sees him in the worst of conditions, and his self will distract him from others. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: They will know each other and recognize each other, then they will flee from each other after that. God the Almighty says: Every person among them, that Day, will have enough to make him indifferent to others. This noble verse is like the Almighty’s saying: “O mankind, fear your Lord and fear a Day when no father will avail his son, nor will a son avail his father at all. Indeed, the promise of God is truth.” And the Almighty’s saying: And if a heavily laden one calls for a load, no one will be able to carry it. Nothing, even if he were a relative.” And as God Almighty said: So when the Trumpet is blown, there will be no kinship between them that Day, nor will they ask about one another. And as God Almighty said: “The Day a man will flee from his brother, * And his mother and his father, * And his wife and his children. * Every man will have, that Day, enough to make him indifferent to God.” And God Almighty said: “The sinner will wish that he could ransom himself from the punishment of that Day with his children, * And his wife and his brother, * And his clan who sheltered him, * And everyone on earth, all together, then he could save him. * No!” That is, no ransom will be accepted from him, even if he came with the people of the earth and the most precious wealth he could find, even if it were the earth full of gold, or with his children who were the contents of his heart in this world. He will wish on the Day of Resurrection, when he sees the horrors, that he could ransom himself from God’s punishment with them, but it will not be accepted from him. Mujahid and As-Suddi said: His clan means his tribe and clan. Ikrimah said: His thigh from which he belongs. Ashhab said on the authority of Malik: His clan means his mother. The Almighty said: Indeed, it is a blazing Fire describing the Fire and its intense heat. Tearing off the skin. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid said: It is the scalp. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Tearing off the skin means the skins and the crown. Mujahid said: The flesh below the bone. Saeed ibn Jubayr said: The nerves and the heel. Abu Salih said: Tearing off the skin means the extremities of the hands and feet. He also said: Tearing off the skin means the flesh of the legs. Al-Hasan Al-Basri and Thabit Al-Bunani said: Tearing off the skin means the noble qualities of his face. Al-Hasan also said: It burns everything in him and his heart remains screaming. Qatadah said: Tearing off the skin means tearing off his crown, the noble qualities of his face, his character and his extremities. Ad-Dahhak said: The meat and skin are removed from the bone until nothing is left. Ibn Zayd said: The roasted meat is the bones. So his saying, Naza’ah, means: Their bones are cut off, then their skins and their creation are changed. God the Almighty says: It calls him who turned back and turned away * And gathered and hoarded. That is, the Fire calls to itself its children whom God created for it, and He decreed that they would do its work in this world, so it will call them on the Day of Resurrection with a fluent, smooth tongue, then it will pick them out from among the people of the gathering place as a bird picks out grain. This is because, as God the Almighty said: They were among those who turned back and turned away, that is, they lied in their hearts and abandoned working with their limbs. And gathered and hoarded. That is, they gathered wealth on top of each other and hoarded it, that is, they stored it up and withheld God's right from it, such as what was required of them in spending and in paying zakat. It was reported in the hadith: Do not hoard, lest God hoard it against you. Abdullah ibn Ukaim would not tie a purse for himself and would say: I heard God say: And gathered and hoarded. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: O son of Adam, you heard God's threat, then the world was hoarded. Qatadah said about His statement: And gathered and hoarded. He said: They were hoarders, rising up against the wicked.

Yes, indeed He is over all things competent. And God the Almighty said in another verse: “Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. * His command when He intends a thing is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is.” And He said here: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that We are surely Able * To substitute better than them, meaning on the Day of Resurrection We will return them with bodies better than these, for His power is suitable for that. And We are not to be outdone, meaning helpless, as God the Almighty said: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are Able to proportion his fingertips. And God the Almighty said: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone * To substitute the likes of you and produce you in that which you do not know. Ibn Jarir chose To substitute better than them, meaning a nation that obeys Us and does not disobey Us, and he made it like His saying: And if We “If you turn away, He will replace you with another people, and they will not be the likes of you. The first meaning is more evident, as other verses indicate it, and God Almighty knows best. Then the Almighty said: So leave them meaning O Muhammad to plunge into vain and play meaning leave them in their denial, disbelief and obstinacy until they meet their promised Day meaning they will know the consequences of that and taste its consequences On the Day they emerge from the graves in haste as if they were, toward a target, hastening meaning: They will rise from the graves when the Lord, Blessed and Exalted be He, calls them to the place of reckoning. 70:44: The Almighty says, denouncing the infidels who were at the time of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and who witnessed him and the guidance that God sent him with and the dazzling miracles with which God supported him. Yet, despite all of this, they were fleeing from him and dispersing from him, straying right and left, groups after groups, and sects after sects, as the Almighty said: Then why do they turn away from the reminder? * As if they were wild donkeys * Fleeing from a lion. This is similar to it, for God the Almighty said: Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they are rushing headlong? That is, what is the matter with these disbelievers who are with you, O Muhammad, that they are rushing headlong, that is, they are quickly fleeing from you, as Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: Rushing headlong means setting off. To the right and to the left in groups. The singular is izza meaning scattered, and it is a state of rushing headlong that is, in the state of their dispersion and disagreement, as Imam Ahmad said about the people of desires, so they are opposing the Book, differing about the Book, and agreeing on opposing the Book. Al-Awfi said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Then what is the matter with those who disbelieved before you that they are rushing headlong, he said, Before you, looking. “To the right and to the left in groups.” He said: The ‘izzin is the group of people, turning to the right and to the left, mocking him. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Bashar told us, Abu ‘Amir told us, Qurra told us on the authority of Al-Hasan regarding his statement: To the right and to the left in groups, that is, scattered, taking to the right and to the left, saying: What did this man say? Qatada said, Rushing deliberately, to the right and to the left in groups, meaning in groups around the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who have no interest in the Book of God or in His Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. Ath-Thawri, Shu’bah, ‘Abtir ibn al-Qasim, ‘Isa ibn Yunus, Muhammad ibn Fadil, Waki’, Yahya al-Qattan, and Abu Mu’awiyah said, all on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Musayyab ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim ibn Tarfa, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to them while they were gathered together and said, Why do I see you gathered together? Narrated by Ahmad, Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Jarir from the hadith of al-A’mash with this chain of narration. Ibn Jarir said, Muhammad ibn Bishr told us, Mu’ammil told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of ‘Abd al-Malik ibn ‘Umair, on the authority of Abu Salamah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to his companions while they were gathered together and said, Why do I see you gathered together? This chain of narration is good, and I have not seen it in any of the six books from this source. God the Almighty says: Does every one of them aspire to enter a garden of pleasure? No! That is, do these people, in this state of their flight from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and their aversion to the truth, aspire to enter the gardens of pleasure? No, rather their refuge is Hell. Then God the Almighty says, confirming the occurrence of the Resurrection and the punishment they denied and ruled out, citing as evidence the beginning, which the return is easier than, and which they acknowledge. God the Almighty says: Indeed, We created them from that which they know. That is, from weak semen, just as God the Almighty said: Did We not create you from a despised water? And He said: “So let man consider from what he was created. He was created from a fluid ejected. Emerging from between the backbone and the ribs. Indeed, he is able to return him. On the Day when secrets will be exposed, he will have no power or helper.” Then God the Almighty says: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests. That is, He who created the heavens and the earth, made the East and the West, and subjected the stars to appear in their Easts and set in their Wests. The meaning of the speech is that the matter is not as you claim, that there is no resurrection, no reckoning, no resurrection, and no rising again. Rather, all of that is real and will inevitably happen. That is why the letter la came at the beginning of the oath to indicate that what is sworn to is negation, which is the meaning of the speech and it is the refutation of their corrupt claim of denying the Day of Resurrection. They have witnessed from the great power of God the Most High what is more eloquent than establishing the Day of Resurrection, which is the creation of the heavens and the earth and the subjection of what is in them of creatures, animals, inanimate objects, and all kinds of existence. That is why God the Most High said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most of mankind do not know. And God the Almighty said: Have they not seen that God, who created the heavens and the earth and was not weary in their creation, is able to give life to the dead? Yes, indeed He is over all things competent. And God the Almighty said in another verse: “Is not He who created the heavens and the earth able to create the likes of them? Yes, and He is the Creator, the Knowing. * His command when He intends a thing is only to say to it, “Be,” and it is.” And He said here: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests that We are surely Able * To substitute better than them, meaning on the Day of Resurrection We will return them with bodies better than these, for His power is suitable for that. And We are not to be outdone, meaning helpless, as God the Almighty said: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones? Yes, We are Able to proportion his fingertips. And God the Almighty said: We have decreed death among you, and We are not to be outdone * To substitute the likes of you and produce you in that which you do not know. The first meaning is more evident, as other verses indicate it, and God Almighty knows best.
